title: Resumable shadow promote with hedged-traffic and scheduled-rollback playbook
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Adds a resumable shadow-to-canary promotion flow with hedged traffic routing and an optional scheduled rollback window; includes playbook and telemetry snapshots for safe promotes.
description: Motivation: teams have asked for a promote flow that lets us seed real traffic via shadowing, then progressively promote (hedged) traffic with the ability to pause/resume and an automated scheduled rollback if safety gates fail. This PR implements a resumable shadow-promote runtime + operator playbook: 1) a shadow seeding controller that can persist a partial promote state (so promotes survive controller restarts), 2) hedged-traffic routing policy that splits live traffic into primary/candidate lanes with configurable hedges and quorum logic, 3) scheduled rollback window support (timeboxed automatic backout if metrics diverge), and 4) telemetry snapshotting at each holdpoint (prefix KV, sample smoke traces, eval set gating). The description below is intentionally linear but the implementation is modular. Changes: - runtime/controller: new shadow_promote controller (resumable state persisted to rollout-store) and hedged router policy (quorum thresholds, hedge_ratio, max_inflight) - api: rollout API extension rollout.spec.promote.strategy = {type: "hedged", hedgeRatio, resumeTokenTTL, scheduledRollback: {enabled, windowMinutes}} - operator/playbooks: add playbook (docs/playbooks/shadow-promote.md) with step-by-step commands to inspect resume tokens, force-finish, or abort promote - telemetry: snapshots recorded to telemetry-store at each holdpoint + smoke-set eval hook; added new metrics: rollout.resume_count, rollout.hedge_confidence, rollout.rollback_trigger_reason - tests: unit tests for state persistence, e2e scenario that simulates controller crash & resume and a scheduled rollback firing Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-2129) [x] unit tests [x] e2e smoke scenario [x] migration path for existing rollout CRDs [x] playbook and quickstart Example config (inline): rollout.spec.promote = {"type":"hedged","hedgeRatio":0.15,"holdpoints":["initial-smoke","telemetry-stable"],"resumeTokenTTL":3600,"scheduledRollback":{"enabled":true,"windowMinutes":30}} Backwards compatibility: default promote behavior unchanged unless strategy=hedged. Rollout store schema change is additive; migration applied via migration/20260214-add-resume-token.sql Note: description compressed into a single paragraph per repo conventions.

review_comments: Maya Kline: Nice end-to-end, but can we avoid a global lock when persisting resume tokens? This will block high-concurrency promotes.
Author (Arjun): Switched to per-rollout lease and sharded store in a follow-up commit (see a1b2c3 -> l4m5n6). Removed global lock and added tests.
Lena Ortiz: The hedged router needs a clearer tie-breaker when quorum is ambiguous (e.g., 50/50). Recommend deterministic tie-breaker based on latency favoring primary.
Author (Arjun): Added hedge_confidence metric and deterministic tie-breaker (latency_pref) with feature flag for teams to opt-out.
Tomás Ruiz: CI flaked on e2e once; reran and passed. Approve after addressing small comments on telemetry retention defaults.
Author (Arjun): Lowered default telemetry snapshot retention to 7 days and added CLI to export snapshots for longer-term SLO debugging. Marking as ready to merge.

notes_on_deploy: Step 1: apply migration migration/20260214-add-resume-token.sql Step 2: deploy controllers (kubectl apply -f deployment/shadow-promote-controller.yaml) Step 3: to kick off hedged promote, POST rollout with strategy=hedged. Inspect resume token: redwoodctl rollout resume-token get <rollout-id>. To force-complete: redwoodctl rollout promote finalize <token>. To abort: redwoodctl rollout promote abort <token>. Scheduled rollback: controller will emit rollout.rollback_triggered metric and perform traffic reversion; operator can disable scheduledRollback in rollout spec to prevent automatic backout.
